objective: Remove host-induced task delays while preserving errors, ordered mutations, cancellation, budgets and independent artifact acceptance.
hypotheses: An ordinary returned failure in a concurrency-safe Bash read need not destroy the useful results of its independent read batch. Preserving them eliminates a recovery round without permitting the next mutation after a failed prerequisite.

A one-second overall deadline for optional file token counting prevents a slow auxiliary endpoint from stopping a local repair task. Conservative byte bounds and smaller-range recovery preserve the file token guard.
scope: Production host components with real files, subprocesses, code repair, independent checkers and local Git delivery. Worker decisions and token-counter service behavior are controlled. This is not a live-model benchmark or a comparison of model intelligence.

design.order: alternate baseline-first and candidate-first by sample; fresh process and workspace for every arm
design.uncompleted_observations: Right-censored at the observation deadline, never assigned a completion time or a speedup ratio.
design.read_service_schedule: The failing optional cat is observed before successful peer receipts are released. No simulated model latency is added. Required file bytes come from real cat subprocesses.

metrics: local Git hook and remote receipt
acceptance: All fault repair tasks independently pass in both arms; candidate uses zero extra read recovery rounds and baseline reproduces at least one.
Healthy task decisions and artifact bytes match; no mutation executes after a failed prerequisite, framework uncertainty or operator cancellation.
Candidate stalled-counter task completes within the fixed observation window using smaller ranges; all unavailable or oversized counts preserve the file token guard.
Focused regressions, affected correctness/command suites, source transpilation, input freeze checks and independent review pass. Missing gates remain explicit.
authority: Local reversible implementation and tests plus public branch and PR publication are authorized by the user. No deployment, published-history rewrite, real third-party messages, credential publication or acceptance weakening.
stop: Stop on unpaired tool receipts, changed frozen inputs, checker tampering, any guardrail regression or unexplained gate failure.
limitations: Selected regression tasks do not estimate production frequency or universal speedup.
No authenticated live GPT-6.1 Sol Max comparison is available.
Task tool service and counter are controlled adapters; full packaged CLI performance is outside this experiment.
